This criminal revision under section 438 read with section 441 of the BNSS, 2023 read with section 102 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 is preferred being aggrieved by order dated 14.08.2024 by the Sessions Judge/ Special Judge, POCSO Act, Neemuch District- Neemuch whereby the claim of juvenility of the revision petitioner apprehended in connection with crime no.316/2024 registered at P.S.- Neemuch City, District-Neemuch (M.P.) under section 363,
366, 376(3) of the IPC, 1860 and sections 4 read with section 3 of the POCSO Act, 2012 has been rejected.

Challenging the impugned order this revision petition is preferred on the ground that trial court committed error in rejecting the applications of the revision petitioner ignoring the birth certificate (Exhibit-A/1) issued by Registrar of Birth and Death, Nagar Palika, Neemuch and duly proved by Registrar AW-2.
Birth certificate (Exhibit-A/1) was issued years before the alleged offence.

Principal Seema Shukla (NAW-1) mentioned the date of birth only on the information of the father of the revision petitioner and no birth certificate or other documents was taken by the school authorities with respect to the age of the revision petitioner.

7. Perused the record.
8.

Trial court has rejected the claim of Juvenility on the ground that when there is conflict between the date of birth recorded in certificate issued by the school in which revision petitioner got admitted in 1st standard and the date of birth recorded in certificate issued by the municipal authorities, then the date of birth recorded in certificate received from the school got preference and court has to presume the correct date of birth as mentioned in the certificate issued by the school and approved the date of birth as correct date mentioned in the school record i.e. 02.05.2005.
Further recorded the finding that revision petitioner has completed the age of 18 years as per section 2 (12) of Juvenile Justice Act, 2015.
9. The correctness of the above finding is being examined and for that purpose the evidence recorded before the trial court is being perused.

Birth certificate (Exhibit-A/1) provided by AW-2 mentions that date of birth was registered on 10.01.2007 and this entry is supported by Exhibit-A/2 i.e. extract of register maintained in District Hospital, Neemuch (M.P.) that have entry to the effect that at 2:30 p.m. of 30.12.2006 a child was born to the AW-2 and vide Exhibit-A/3 the birth of revision petitioner on 30.12.2006 was intimated to the Registrar of Birth and Death of M.P. on 10.01.2007 and the same was registered at Sl. No.414 of the register.
NEUTRAL
CITATION

Witness Umesh Yadav Inspector of Police examined as NAW-2 has admitted in para-8 that he himself procured the date of birth certificate from Municipal Corporation Neemuch and the date of birth of the revision petitioner in the certificate was mentioned as 30.12.2006.
Seema Shukla NA- 1 admitted that when revision petitioner was admitted in their school then no birth certificate of the revision petitioner was received by the school.

In this case, Principal, Seema Shukla (NA-1) has mentioned that date of birth of the revision petitioner was recorded in the scholar register as 02.05.2005 on the information of father and Exhibit-N/3 was obtained from the father of the revision petitioner but PW-1 has stated that they went tot the school for admitting the revision Govind vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 24 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117509656/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2 petitioner then the date of birth was entered by the concerned teacher as per his guess.

Revision petitioner was admitted in school on 21.06.2011 and on the basis of date of birth 30.12.2016,
revision petitioner's age is 4 years 6 months and 23 days.
So it cannot be said that as per the date of birth 30.12.2006 the revision petitioner have not attained the age that he could be admitted in school.

Accordingly, the date of birth recorded in Exhibit-N/1 is not proved and we have to assess the date of birth on the strength of the documents mentioned in clause (ii) of Section 94 (2) of Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 and that documents Annexure-A/1 issued by the Registrar of Birth and Death, Nagar Palika Nigam, Neemuch (M.P.) proved through Mahesh Ramani (PW-2) &
corroborated by P/2 (certificate issued by maternity in-charge, District Hospital Neemuch) and Exhibit-A/3 the intimation of the date of birth of the revision petitioner on 10.01.2007 establishes the date of birth of revision petitioner as 30.12.2006.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:37833 5 CRR-5420-2024 11.

Accordingly, trial court committed error in discarding the claim of juvenility of the revision petitioner on the basis of date of birth of 30.12.2006 and assessing the age of the revision petitioner above 18 years only on the ground that Annexure-N/1 falls within clause (i) of section 94 (2) of Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 whereas the birth certificate (Exhibit-A/1) comes in clause (ii) of section 94 (2) of Juvenile Justice Act, 2015.
This interpretation would have been correct if the document N/1 would have been proved through cogent evidence.
But in this case, that document has not been proved either through the person who recorded the date of birth or by the persons who got admitted the child in the school.

Hence order dated 14.08.2024 by the Sessions Judge/ Special Judge, POCSO Act, Neemuch (Annexure-A/1) suffers from illegality and could not be sustained and accordingly it is hereby set aside and the date of birth of the revision petitioner is determined as 30.12.2006.
Trial court is directed to proceed further in the case treating the date of birth of the revision petitioner as 30.12.2006 and decide the applications afresh.
12. With the aforesaid, revision petition is allowed and disposed off.
13. Trial court is directed to ensure the supply of copy of this order to the victim in the light of Aparna Bhat vs. State of M.P - AIR 2021 SC 1492 .
